name: Front terrace

dimensions.notes: Measured by the owners: 120 cm from wall to railings, almost 5 m long.

orientation: Street-facing, full width of the façade, balustrade with two piers

photos.caption: Mountain end: two bistro chairs and table, orange downpipe, weathered wall
Barbecue end: charcoal barbecue, TV aerial mast with trailing cables, mould-stained end wall, wooden shutter on the lounge doors
The lounge doors from outside — painted green

current.summary: Long, narrow terrace across the front of the top floor: 1.20 m deep and almost 5 m long, reached through the lounge's double doors (green outside, with wooden shutters). Red quarry-tile floor, iron railings between rendered piers. Mountain end: two folding bistro chairs and a small table, facing the rock face and the village. Other end: a charcoal barbecue, the TV aerial mast with cables trailing down the wall and across the floor, and a mould-stained end wall. House wall: old textured render, weathered and stained, with patches; new dark metal gutter and fascia at the eaves; orange PVC downpipe; small solar light.
keep: The views: village, church and the mountain

Proposed by Claude (not yet agreed): TV aerial mast and trailing cables — move, tidy or remove (is it still used now there is a satellite dish?)
Proposed by Claude (not yet agreed): Loose cable across the floor — trip hazard

target.concept: DRAFT — the view terrace. Keep it simple and narrow-friendly: a slim bench or two bistro chairs and a small round table at the mountain end for morning coffee and sunset drinks, a row of terracotta pots (geraniums, herbs, a small olive) along the railing base, the wall cleaned and painted warm white, and the downpipe and antenna dealt with so nothing interrupts the view.
target.renderPrompt:
Edit this photo of a room in our house. Keep the exact camera angle and keep all the architecture exactly as it is — walls, room shape, windows, doors, beams, floor and fixed fittings. Do not add, move or remove anything structural, and do not change the furniture unless I say so below. Remove all clutter: tools, boxes, bags, dust sheets, loose cables, packaging, laundry and toiletries. Show the room finished and tidy.

Changes to make:
- Keep the red tile floor, the iron railings between the piers, the two bistro chairs and table, and the mountain view.
- House wall cleaned, repaired and painted warm white — no mould, stains or patches.
- The orange downpipe painted to match the wall. No TV aerial and no cables on the wall or floor.
- Railings and pier caps freshly painted, railings black.
- A row of terracotta pots with red geraniums and herbs along the base of the railing. Morning light.

Style: photorealistic interior photograph, natural light plus warm 2700K lamps, no people, no text or labels.
